en: The Questions of King Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes, Part One:
The Earth Section
4. The Question on Wind “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘five qualities of wind should be adopted,’ which are those five qualities that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, wind blows through the midst of a forest grove in full bloom;”
In the same way, great king, the yogin, the practitioner of yoga, should delight in the midst of the forest of objects that have blossomed with the choice flowers of liberation.
This, great king, is the first quality of the wind to be adopted.
Furthermore, great king, the wind agitates the multitudes of trees growing from the earth.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga who has gone into the forest and is investigating conditioned phenomena must churn away the defilements.
This, Great King, is the second quality of wind that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, wind moves through space.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner engaged in yoga should direct the mind toward supramundane states.
This, Great King, is the third quality of wind that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, wind experiences fragrance.
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, the yogāvacara, should experience the fragrant scent of the excellence of his own virtue.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality of the wind that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the wind has no abode and dwells without a home.
In the same way, Great King, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should be without abode, without home, without intimacy, and liberated in every respect.
This, Great King, is the fifth quality of the wind that should be adopted.
And this, Great King, was spoken by the Blessed One, the God above Gods, in the *Sutta Nipāta*:
“From intimacy fear is born;
from a home, dust arises.
Without a home and without intimacy—”
“This indeed is the vision of a sage.
Thus ends the fourth inquiry, the Question of Vāyuṅga.
